MUSA 5500 and MUSA 6950 · Fall 2026 final project

## The project

An accessory dwelling unit (ADU) is a small second home on a house lot: a backyard cottage, a unit over a garage, or an apartment inside the house.
Two Pennsylvania bills would open ADUs statewide, HB 2186 and SB 1346. Philadelphia has its own bill, 250042. None of them is law. The state session ends Nov 30, 2026.

The tool answers three questions for one lot, under today's law and under each reform:

- **Is it allowed?** Rule files with cited sections for Philadelphia, Pittsburgh and 36 more municipalities, and a statewide baseline for the rest.
- **Does it fit?** A geometry test on the lot, building and street outlines, with the setbacks from the rules. Land cover from aerial images adds trees and open ground as context.
- **Does it pay off?** Itemised build costs and local rents, and a tract-level test of where a unit covers its loan.

[Open the tool](tool.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}
[Tract explorer](musa5500/figures/tract_explorer.html){.btn .btn-outline-primary}

Not legal advice. Not a zoning determination. Parcel lines are not a survey.

## Two classes, one tool

| | MUSA 5500 | MUSA 6950 |
|---|---|---|
| Question | Where is there demand, and where does an ADU pay off? | What is on the lot, and is there room? |
| Methods | Census and ACS APIs, margins of error, K-means vs GMM vs Ward, gradient boosting with county-held-out tests, payoff test, scenario arithmetic | U-Net land cover on 4-band NAIP, fair comparison of model variants, error analysis, transfer to two cities, outbuilding detector, vector fit test |
| Tool mode | ADU projecting and analysis | ADU Testing |
| Pages | [Proposal](musa5500/docs/proposal.md) · [Data](musa5500/docs/data.md) · [Methods](musa5500/docs/methods.md) · [Results](musa5500/docs/results.md) | [Proposal](musa6950/docs/proposal.md) · [Data](musa6950/docs/data.md) · [Methods](musa6950/docs/methods.md) · [Results](musa6950/docs/results.md) |

## Results in short

<!-- source: ~/musa-drive/lots/pittsburgh/stats.json (data version pittsburgh-20261111-bdeb5697ae), ~/musa-drive/lots/philadelphia/stats.json (data version philadelphia-20261111-b7fa7bda07), ~/musa-drive/models/*/test_scores.json, ~/musa-drive/processed/5500/payoff_summary.json and forecast_summary.json, shared/rules/towns_index.json -->

| Result | Value |
|---|---|
| Philadelphia lots with any legal ADU path today | 1.2%<!-- stats.json all.allowed_today --> of 459,998 |
| Pittsburgh lots with any legal ADU path today | 100% of 92,081 (a detached unit needs an Administrator's Exception) |
| Pittsburgh lots where a 600 sq ft detached unit fits today | 41.2% |
| Land cover U-Net, test mIoU on held-out counties | about 0.70 (no run reached 0.72 mIoU or 0.65 building IoU) |
| Tracts where a 600 sq ft 1-bedroom unit pays off (mid cost) | 10.3% (356 of 3,445) |
| ADUs by 2031, mid case | about 1,000 today, about 13,500 with HB 2186, about 13,200 with SB 1346 |
| Lots with room for a 600 sq ft unit, statewide | about 2.9 million (1.5 to 3.6 million). Measured in Philadelphia and Pittsburgh, modelled elsewhere |
| Of the 36 next-largest municipalities, no ADU text in the code | 17 |

The binding limit differs by city. In Philadelphia it is the law. In Pittsburgh every lot has a legal path, and the limit is yard space.

## What is not measured yet

- The fit answers have not been checked against hand labels. The 250-lot sample is drawn and none are labeled.
- The outbuilding detector is scored only against unchecked first-pass labels.

## Code and docs

The code, the pipeline docs and the model cards are in the [repository](https://github.com/yezhanggg/YZ-MUSA-FINAL). Each class has its own folder: `musa5500/` and `musa6950/`.
